run.change_description: lib/batcher: prevent commits racing shutdown - fixes #9687

summary.intent: Close a channel-ordering race in lib/batcher where a Commit could pass the closed-check and then have its request land in the input channel behind the shutdown quit marker, leaving a synchronous caller blocked forever and silently dropping an async upload.
summary.issue_fit: Full — admission is now serialized with shutdown's close-and-quit-send under one mutex, so every accepted commit is either enqueued strictly before the quit marker (and thus processed) or rejected with the pre-existing shutdown error; the fix adds no new externally observable behavior.
summary.coverage: Both changed files read in full at head and compared against the merge-base; the package's tests, including the new race regression test, ran offline with -race and passed; go vet is clean.
check_details: Reviewer ran `go test -count=1 -race ./lib/batcher` at 0b87bc4788cd50664b82dd7e74c78aa2c7fc3b1c offline: pass (`ok  github.com/rclone/rclone/lib/batcher  5.332s`), exercising TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown's sync and async subtests.
Reviewer ran `go vet ./lib/batcher` at the same head: clean, no output.

The PR-claimed `go test -race ./lib/batcher -count=20`, `go build`, and `make quicktest` supply no readable output and were not independently reproduced at that scope; the reviewer-executed race run above already covers the same test.

observations.fact: Commit's admission critical section under the new admitMu also now covers the pre-existing `fs.Debugf(b.f, "Adding %q to batch", name)` call, so a slow `Stringer.String()` on the batching identity would hold admission (and block Shutdown) longer than before this change.
observations.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:267-281; production `fs.Fs` identities passed as `f` are cheap strings, so no concrete instance is shown to matter.

requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:50 (admitMu field), :243 and :252 (Shutdown locks admitMu around close(b.closed) and the quit send), :267,:271,:281 (Commit locks admitMu around its closed-check and its send) — every accepted commit is enqueued strictly before the quit marker or explicitly rejected.

requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:243-252 and :267-281 pair Shutdown's close+quit-send and Commit's check+send under one mutex.

requirements.source: spec-pr9699-packet/pr-body/"Preserve the existing shutdown error for commits that arrive after shutdown starts."
requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher.go:269-271 returns the same `fserrors.FatalError(errors.New("batcher is shutting down"))` text and type as the merge-base (`git show 862ed2b7a:lib/batcher/batcher.go` lines 262-264), unchanged.

requirements.source: spec-pr9699-packet/pr-body/"Add regression coverage for synchronous hangs and asynchronous dropped uploads."
requirements.evidence: lib/batcher/batcher_test.go TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown (sync and async subtests) uses a blockingStringer to deterministically pause Commit between its closed-check and its send while Shutdown races it, then asserts no hang via 1s timeouts and that the admitted item was actually committed via the `committed` channel; traced the mechanism against both the fixed code (passes) and the base code (the paused commit's send would land after commitLoop already exited on the quit message, reproducing the hang/drop).
